Reducing the pool to the most informative models (pool5) also mitigates the high variance of weight estimation that comes from having only three validation windows.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate A, while having a very low first‑window error, suffers from a large second‑window error (1.6109) and a higher overall score (0.1928). Its forward‑selection weights on the full pool may overfit the limited validation data. Candidate C has the worst overall score (0.2124) and a larger second‑window error (1.7634); its inverse‑error weights on the full pool with shrinkage do not compensate for the high variance in this series. Therefore, B is the most reliable choice for generalization to the blind test window.
